explanation: Bounds reusable terminal scratch independently of its absolute placement. The zero-based extent can be translated to an arbitrary work pointer without changing its relative quadratic bound.
theorem_title: A quadratic cell bound for terminal reporting
theorem_formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.wanted_terminal_cells_le (n : ℕ) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightReportingTerminal.space 0 (_root_.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.half n) (_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.blocks n)≤20*(_root_.ThreeSum.SharedReportingBankResourceBounds.magnitude n+1)^2 := by sorry
theorem_natural_language_statement:
At natural input size $n$, terminal reporting from relative work base zero, evaluated at the executable local half-size and block count, satisfies $$\operatorname{terminalSpace}(0)\le20(M(n)+1)^2.$$ Here $M$ is the reporting magnitude envelope.

Bounds reusable terminal scratch independently of its absolute placement. This supports the complete deterministic integer 3SUM runtime proof.
